To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tropopause is constrained by thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere to be at roughly the same altitude and temperature throughout the globe, that the temperature of the upper troposphere and the temperature of the tropopause are both constrained by the thermodynamic properties of atmospheric water vapor, that the amplitude of large scale dynamics in the extratropical troposphere is also constrained by the thermodynamics of atmospheric water vapor.
the thermodynamic properties of moist air strongly constrain the depth and temperature of the troposphere and the temperature of high-altitude clouds throughout the globe.
the depth of the tropical troposphere is constrained by the same fundamental thermodynamic properties as the tropical anvil temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical factors governing the vertical structure of the troposphere and the amplitude of the large-scale circulation throughout the globe.
the physical mechanisms that govern the depth and amplitude dynamics in the troposphere.
understanding the physical processes governing the depth of the planetary tropospheric circulation and how these processes respond to climate change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tropopause temperature, the depth of the tropical tropopause, the cloud-top temperature, and the amplitude (or strength) of the large-scale dynamics in the extratropical tropics are constrained by the thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere, and in particular by the rapid decrease of the saturation vapor pressure with height.

the thermodynamic properties of the troposphere are constrained by the saturation vapor pressure of water, and the depth of the tropical troposphere is constrained by the same thermodynamic properties of vapor.
the depth of the tropical troposphere is constrained by the fundamental properties of water vapor in the tropics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the depth of the atmosphere, the temperature of the tropopause, and the temperature of high-altitude clouds are strongly constrained by thermodynamic properties of moist air, and are not significantly affected by changes in the concentration of greenhouse gases.
the thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere constrain the depth and amplitude, but not the structure, of the large-scale circulation throughout the globe.
the troposphere is a thermodynamic entity that is constrained by the basic thermodynamic properties of the water vapor and the Clausius-Clapeyron relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the troposphere is a single thermodynamic system, and that the same basic physical factors that govern tropical high clouds also govern the depth and temperature of the troposphere throughout the globe.
the tropopause temperature and cloud-top temperature are strongly constrained by basic thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere and should not change significantly in a warmer climate.

the depth of the atmosphere, the tropopause temperature, the temperature of the top of the atmosphere, and the temperature of high cloud decks are all strongly constrained by the basic thermodynamic properties of the atmosphere, namely, the saturation water vapor pressures and the Clausius-Clapeyron equation.
